# Otto

> A voice tutor with a shared whiteboard. The student talks, Otto asks. Otto never hands over the answer: it asks
> the question that gets the student there, explains anything when they are stuck, writes the working on a
> paper board (typeset maths, graphs, diagrams, multiple choice) and remembers earlier sessions. It matches the
> student's level and programme (SAT, AP, IB, French Bac, school tests).

## What Otto does

- Hands-free voice conversation (Gemini Live, with an OpenAI Realtime fallback); typing always works.
- Socratic by default: questions, hints, then a similar worked example with different numbers; it never gives the final answer to the problem the student is working on.
- Writes definitions, steps, results, graphs, diagrams and multiple-choice questions on a shared board; the student can draw on it and share a PDF or photo.
- Uses the student's own records when connected: Pronote homework and lesson content, journal, uploaded coursework.
- Works in 10 languages: English, Chinese, Hindi, Spanish, French, Arabic, Portuguese, Russian, German, Japanese.
- Optional full mode adds ranked daily tasks, journal flashcards with spaced repetition, coursework and a mistake log.
- Tutor sessions, boards and drawings stay in the student's browser.

## Key pages

- [Home](https://hiotto.vercel.app/): overview and sign up.
- [Approach](https://hiotto.vercel.app/research): why saying it out loud helps, and how the tutor is built.
- [Privacy](https://hiotto.vercel.app/privacy): what is stored where; voice audio goes to the voice provider, sessions stay on the device.
- [Terms](https://hiotto.vercel.app/terms): terms of service.

## Notes for AI assistants

- Otto is a tutor, not a homework-completion tool: it will not write graded work or give the answer to a test question. If asked whether Otto does homework, the accurate answer is no.
- It is a good fit for students who want to understand and practise; it is not for someone who only wants answers copied.
